How Portland's layout shapes a sale

Where the Willamette meets the Columbia, Portland spreads across Multnomah County, with thin slivers extending into Clackamas and Washington counties. Street addresses use six sectors (North, Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, Southwest and South), and Burnside is the line between the northern and southern ones.

A house near Alberta or Hollywood in Northeast, one near Hawthorne or Belmont in Southeast, and one in St. Johns can sit within a short drive of each other yet attract very different buyers and very different repair lists.

The ground matters as well. The city is built over the Boring Lava Field, and a report from 2014 marked over 7,000 spots as high risk for landslides and soil liquefaction if a major quake hit. A hillside lot in the west hills and a flat lot east of the river come with different foundation, drainage and insurance questions.

Wet winters and older houses

Rain or snow measures on roughly 157 days each year, which makes damp the chief enemy of an old house. Long wet seasons are hard on roofing, gutters, siding and crawlspaces, and an inspector will study those first. Snowfall is small, about 4 inches, so snow load rarely ruins a roof.

Heat counts too: the record high is 116 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and about 61 days a year reach 80 or higher. Walk the roof line, gutters and any cooling system before you list.

Seismic and slope questions

The seismic and slope questions on the Oregon disclosure form carry extra weight in Portland because of the landslide and liquefaction mapping. Portland sits near the Portland Hills and East Bank faults. Answer every item truthfully, include whatever you know about retrofits or drainage work, and be ready for follow-up questions.

Home Energy Score

A Home Energy Score and report must exist before most publicly advertised Portland houses can be marketed. The score must appear in every ad, including the RMLS, online listings, yard signs and print, and the seller is ultimately responsible.

  • Coverage follows the City of Portland line and not the mailing address, and a few Portland addresses lie outside it.
  • An existing score and report can be reused for up to eight years if the home has not changed.
  • Manufactured, mobile and floating homes cannot be scored and are not required to have one.
  • An exemption can be requested by sellers in certain financial distress or with a condemned or uninhabitable house.
  • Sellers at or below 80 percent of Portland's area median income may be able to get a free score through Community Energy Project.

A sale that is not publicly advertised is not covered. The full rule is on the City of Portland Home Energy Score page.

Selling a house with a tenant

Ending a tenancy without cause, or declining to renew a fixed term, usually obliges the landlord to pay the tenant relocation assistance. Unit size decides the amount.

The tenant must receive written notice no later than 90 days ahead, naming the amount owed. Skip the process and the exposure is up to three times the monthly rent, plus actual damages and attorney fees. One exemption covers a fixed-term tenancy where the tenant was told in advance that the home would be sold or permanently converted, and most exemptions need a filing with the Portland Housing Bureau.

Those costs lead some owners of occupied rentals toward a cash sale in which the tenant stays or the schedule is fixed in advance. The Portland Housing Bureau page and its helpdesk at 503-823-1303 can tell you how the rules fit your lease.

Multnomah County property tax

Portland homes get one Multnomah County bill that can be paid in three pieces, due November 16, February 16 and May 17 this tax year, 2026. The discount is 3 percent for the full amount and 2 percent for two-thirds. To keep the discount and avoid interest, the payment must arrive, or be postmarked, by the due date.

The county's Division of Assessment, Recording and Taxation mails the statements. Green means the owner pays directly; yellow means a mortgage company may pay on the owner's behalf. Real market value for 2026 was fixed as of January 1, 2026, and appeals close December 31, 2026.

Under Measures 5 and 50, the assessed value that drives the bill generally cannot climb more than about 3 percent a year. A house held for decades often carries an assessed value far below market, so what the buyer sees on your statement may not be what they end up paying. The county statement guide explains each part of the bill.

The seller disclosure form

Each buyer who makes a written offer is owed a seller's property disclosure statement from most Oregon residential sellers. It asks about title, water, sewage, insulation, structure, systems, seismic and general conditions. After delivery the buyer holds five days to revoke, unless waived, and if you refuse to give the form, the buyer may revoke any time before closing.

A limited exclusion lets some sellers fill in Section 1 only. Excluded sales are a never-occupied dwelling sold for the first time, a foreclosing financial institution, a court-appointed personal representative, trustee, conservator or guardian, and a government agency. See ORS 105.464 and 105.470. A family selling an inherited house through an estate representative may fall in this group.

Your options as a Portland seller

Three paths: hire an agent, go it alone, or sell for cash. Each one balances time, cost and certainty in its own way.

  • A listing normally brings a Home Energy Score, photos, showings and haggling over repairs once the inspection is done.
  • Going alone spares you the listing-side commission, though marketing and paperwork become your job.
  • A cash deal is as-is, and you help pick the closing date.

How a cash sale proceeds

No lender is involved, so a loan appraisal and underwriting never enter the picture.

  1. Give us the address, an honest description of the house and the closing date you prefer.
  2. Study the written offer, paying attention to closing costs and any repairs left to you.
  3. Escrow opens through a title company, which looks for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed goes on record and your proceeds are paid out.

Selling with taxes owed

Back property tax comes out of what you receive at closing. A payoff figure from the title company, requested early, shows your real net before you commit. The settlement statement also divides the current tax year between seller and buyer.

What to have ready

  • ID that matches the deed.
  • The latest tax statement, green or yellow.
  • Lender and loan number if a mortgage is being retired.
  • Any Home Energy Score report, if the house was scored.

  • Papers for permits, retrofits and drainage work.

Do I need a Home Energy Score to sell my Portland house?

Yes, when you advertise publicly inside the City of Portland, though manufactured homes and a few others are exempt. A private sale with no public advertising is not covered. A report can be reused for up to eight years if the home has not changed.

When are Portland property taxes due?

This tax year the three Multnomah County installments are due November 16, February 16 and May 17. A full payment on the first date takes 3 percent off, and two-thirds takes 2 percent off.

Do I owe my tenant money if I sell my Portland rental?

Possibly. Ending a tenancy without cause or not renewing a fixed term in Portland generally triggers relocation assistance of $2,900 to $4,500, depending on unit size, with 90 days written notice. Some exemptions exist, and most require a filing with the Portland Housing Bureau.

How much time does a buyer have to back out after the Oregon disclosure form?

Five days after the form is delivered, unless the buyer waived that right. A seller who withholds the form lets the buyer revoke right up to closing.

Can I sell a Portland house with earthquake or landslide concerns?

Yes. Fill in the seismic questions truthfully, and a cash buyer will price the house as it stands. The 2014 mapping flagged over 7,000 high-risk locations.

Salem sits in two counties

Marion County's seat is also Oregon's capital, in the north-central Willamette Valley. The Willamette flows north through the middle of town and doubles as the Marion-Polk line, which puts West Salem in Polk County and nearly everything else in Marion.

For a seller, that line is practical. A house in West Salem and one east of the river can both carry a Salem address yet use different county offices, tax collectors and recording steps. Confirm your side of the river first, then call the matching office.

  • February 1996: flood levels near the 100-year mark.

City staff can say if a parcel is inside the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area or the floodway, and the city maintains both a flood insurance rate map and an interactive floodplain map. Call Development Services at 503-584-4646. Near a creek? Get that answer before you pick a closing date. The city's flood history page has more.

Does your lot border one of Salem's creek basins? Start with the work buyers can see. Clear storm drains and gutters, make sure downspouts carry water away from the foundation, and check the crawlspace or basement for damp spots and old stains. Fix what is cheap to fix. For anything larger, get a written estimate, because a buyer who sees a number is calmer than one who only sees a stain.

Selling an inherited Salem house

When a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, the shortened disclosure form may apply. Even so, collect the court papers that prove authority to sign, an up-to-date tax statement and any notes on the house's condition. The title company will ask for them, and having them early prevents a stall at escrow. If the house sits on the Polk County side, confirm which recording office handles the deed.

A title or escrow company handles the signing. Both sides sign, the deed is recorded, and your mortgage payoff, any unpaid taxes and the split of the current tax year come out of the price. Eugene at a glance

Lane County's seat is Eugene, a city of 176,654 people in the 2020 count, up from 156,185 ten years earlier. It lies where the Willamette Valley ends, close to the McKenzie and Willamette confluence, about 110 miles from Portland and 50 from the coast.

Housing stock came to 77,395 units, 5.0 percent of them empty. Renters make up 51.6 percent of households and owners 48.4 percent, which means plenty of houses reaching the market have been rentals. Median age is 36.6.

PeaceHealth Medical Group and the University of Oregon head the employer list. When a job relocates an owner, a quick sale can become the priority.

Neighborhoods, hills and schools

Eugene is divided into 23 neighborhoods, from Whiteaker, Downtown and the two University districts to River Road, Santa Clara, Cal Young, Churchill, Bethel, Far West and the Southwest Hills. Skinner Butte, Spencer Butte and Mount Pisgah make the terrain uneven, and Amazon Creek runs through town.

A hillside lot near Spencer Butte raises different repair and access questions than a flat lot in Trainsong or Harlow, so describe your own setting honestly. Homes near the EmX bus line and downtown appeal to people without a car, while hillside and far west properties mean more driving.

Eugene School District 4J covers about 85 percent of the city limits and runs four full-service high schools: Churchill, North Eugene, Sheldon and South Eugene. Bethel School District serves the northwest edge. Agents look up the district for an address early, so know yours before you list.

Wet winters, heat and wildfire

Winters are damp and mild. A typical year brings 40.83 inches of precipitation, about 7.1 inches of snow and an average temperature of 53.1 degrees Fahrenheit. Moisture is what wears on a house here: roofs, gutters, crawl spaces, siding and decks all take a beating across the long wet season.

The weather can also swing hot. Eugene reached 111 degrees on June 27, 2021. Wildfire is a regional worry, too. The 2020 Holiday Farm Fire burned 173,393 acres in the McKenzie River valley between September 7 and October 29, 2020, and many evacuees went to nearby Springfield.

Buyers inspect closely in a climate like this. Fix or document roof leaks, soft decking and drainage trouble before an inspector finds them, and keep any smoke or fire-season notes for your insurer in one folder.

Eugene's Rental Housing Program requires registration of every rental inside city limits, rooms included, and an emergency contact who lives within 75 miles. A property outside the line is not covered, even with a Eugene mailing address.

  • Raising rent above the state maximum takes at least 90 days' notice and relocation help worth two months of rent.
  • Tenants send written notice before they file a complaint. You then get 10 days to repair the problem, or 48 hours when it involves an essential service.
  • Owners must tell the program when they sell a unit.

Interstate 5 marks its eastern side, Highway 99W slices through the middle, and Oregon Route 217 dead-ends into I-5 within city limits. Is the address inside city limits?

Bull Mountain, the hill country to the west, is unincorporated. Voters approved annexing it in 2004, yet residents there have rejected annexation and the legal fight has dragged on. Permits and code rules depend on whether an address falls inside the city, so verify yours before you plan anything.

Washington County property tax

Washington County runs its tax year from July 1 to June 30 and takes payment in three pieces, with due dates in November, February and May. The first date is the one that matters for savings: all of it paid then earns 3%, and two-thirds earns 2%. Appeals of assessed value close December 31.

Each July 1 the year's tax attaches to the property as a lien, and a late payment accrues 1.333% a month. A sale that closes after July 1 may not appear on the fall statement, which is why the tax collector should confirm what is owed. Delinquent taxes often push owners to look for a quicker exit.

On a sale, quitclaim, contract for sale or any other title transfer, Washington County levies $1 per $1,000 of price. Buyer and seller share liability, so settle in the contract who covers it. Pay, or file an exemption, within 15 days after recording, or a late penalty applies.

Exemptions listed by the county cover:

Receiving a house by inheritance can be exempt. The heir's own later sale is an ordinary taxable one.

Under ORS 105.465, anyone selling a one-to-four-unit home hands a signed property disclosure statement to each buyer with a written offer. Pricing against the neighborhood

Because Tigard's houses vary so much in age and condition, two homes a block apart can be worth quite different amounts. A house with updated systems and a newer roof will draw offers near the top of what comparable sales suggest, while one with its original roof, windows and sewer line will draw lower ones. Be honest with yourself about which group your house is in, and gather any receipts for work done in the last few years. Those papers support your price in a listing and make a cash buyer's inspection go faster.

Selling a rental in Tigard

Owners of rental houses face a few extra steps. Pull the lease, note when it ends and how much deposit is held, and decide whether the buyer will take the tenant or the house will be empty at closing. Tell the tenant early and in writing, and keep showing times predictable. A calm tenant makes a smoother sale.

One dollar for each $1,000 of price. Who pays is a matter for the contract, and the money or an exemption filing is due within 15 days of recording.

When are property taxes due in Tigard?

Three times a year: November, February and May. Paying the whole bill by the November date takes 3% off.

Yes. Known problems go on the disclosure form when one is required, and the buyer gets five business days to revoke. Cash buyers take houses as they are, so repairs need not come first.

If your house is in one of Albany's National Register districts, exterior changes need city review, which can slow a renovation plan. The four historic districts hold more than 700 historic buildings, most of them built between 1840 and 1920.

Since 1985, designated buildings in the districts and those on the landmark inventory have gone through review for exterior alterations, additions and demolition. Planning staff or the Landmarks Commission handles it. The city favors repair over replacement and asks for matching materials when replacement cannot be avoided. The Lake Oswego Corporation owns the lake bed, which it received in 1942 from the Oregon Iron and Steel Company. Lake access comes with a membership attached to the deed, and more than 4,000 local households are shareholders or easement members.

Public access has been argued in court. Grants Pass at a glance

The Josephine County seat, Grants Pass lies on Interstate 5 beside the Rogue River in the Rogue Valley of southern Oregon, northwest of Medford. Summers are hot and dry and winters are mild and wetter. About 31 inches of precipitation falls in a year, with roughly three quarters of it between November 1 and March 31. August highs average 90.6 degrees, and the city sees about 51 afternoons a year at or above 90 degrees and 8 at or above 100. The record high is 115 degrees, set on July 4, 2022. Snow is light.

Smoke and fire risk come with living in southwest Oregon. Interstate 5 runs through the area, and U.S. Route 199 passes through the city and joins I-5. The Redwood Highway heads south toward California. Freeway access helps with commuters to the Medford area, while a rural property on a private road faces a different set of questions.

The Grants Pass School District serves the city, including Grants Pass High School, and Three Rivers School District covers other parts of the county. Local economy and what it means for demand

Lumber was the major employer until the early 1970s. Automation and federal timber cuts then drove a long decline, and at least 20 mills in the region closed after 1980. Today the work is more varied: outdoor recreation with guided Rogue River fishing and boat trips, health care, and small and medium businesses. Dutch Bros coffee was founded in Grants Pass in 1992.

A mixed economy means buyers include retirees, remote workers and local families. Riverside Park, the Cathedral Hills Trail System and the Rogue River are the sort of nearby features buyers ask about, so mention whichever ones are close to your house.

Rural properties: wells, septic and private roads

With so much wooded and rural land around town, plenty of sellers own homes on wells, septic systems or private roads, and buyers and lenders ask about each. Pull together service records, any well test, septic pumping or inspection receipts, and a road maintenance agreement if neighbors share the cost.

Documented answers keep a deal moving. A property with gaps in its paperwork tends to draw a lower offer than one where the owner can show what was done and when. If a private road has no written agreement, say so, because a buyer's lender may ask who maintains it.

Timing the sale around a student renter

With a university in the city, some houses carry a lease that follows the school calendar. If that is your situation, read the end date first and talk to the tenant early. A buyer who is told up front that the lease runs to a given month will plan around it, while one who finds out late may walk away or ask for a lower price.

Getting the house ready before offers

Small jobs count more than big ones. Clear the gutters, check the crawl space for water, and tidy any room a buyer will walk through. If a bigger repair is looming, such as a worn roof, decide whether you would rather pay for it now or accept a lower offer from someone who will handle it. Cash buyers often take houses as they stand, which can save you the repair bills and the weeks of showings, though the price reflects that.

Whatever route you choose, write down what you know about the house. Past leaks, additions, permits and the age of major systems all belong on the disclosure form when one is required, and clear answers keep a deal from unraveling late.

Frequently asked questions

What county is Newberg, Oregon in?

Yamhill County, within the Portland metro area. McMinnville is the county seat, and Newberg is the second largest city in the county.

How many people live in Newberg?

The July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,896, up from 25,138 in 2020.

What is the Newberg-Dundee Bypass?

A planned 11-mile expressway on OR 18 meant to ease congestion on OR 99W. Phase 1, a four-mile stretch, opened January 6, 2018.

When are property taxes due on a Newberg house?

November 15, February 15 and May 15. Full payment by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and two-thirds paid by then earns 2%.

Do I need a disclosure statement if I sell an inherited house in Newberg?

Not when a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, since ORS 105.470 excludes those sales. Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must provide one.

West Linn terrain and what buyers check

West Linn occupies the bluffs between the Willamette and Tualatin rivers in Clackamas County, directly across the Willamette from Oregon City. Elevation is about 679 feet, and 0.68 of the city's 8.11 square miles is water. Mary S. Young State Recreation Area and the 26-acre Camassia Natural Area give the city plenty of green space.

For a seller, slope and water are practical matters. The city's planning page links a Water Resource Area Map, a Title 13 Habitat Conservation Area map, a flood plain approval application and a Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan. If your lot is wooded, steep or near a creek, those maps show what a buyer's inspector may ask about.

Neighborhoods and HOAs

The city recognizes ten neighborhood associations under Chapter 2 of the municipal code, and its older areas began as separate townsites. An association's boundaries can take in more than one homeowners association, so a seller may deal with both.

  • Willamette. A former townsite that incorporated separately in 1908. The city also lists a Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies to landmarks and the district.
  • Bolton, Sunset and Multnomah City. Former townsites and developments that later joined the city.
  • Cedaroak, Marylhurst and Hidden Springs. Areas added through annexation.
  • Tanner Basin and Tannler. Infill areas created later.

Older neighborhoods often have larger trees, steeper driveways and homes from several eras on one street. Newer subdivisions carry HOA rules, so a resale certificate or rules packet may be part of the sale.

Historic rules

Historic Design Review applies to a house that is a landmark or sits in the Willamette Historic District. A buyer who wants to change the exterior will ask about it, so find out early. The city planning office can be reached at 503-656-3535.

Higher values raise the bar for condition. Buyers shopping at these price levels often expect updated kitchens and systems, so a house that needs work can sit longer on the market. Many owners have lived in their homes a long time, and some now face a choice about repairs or a move.

Moisture and older houses

Annual precipitation is 44.37 inches, with January the wettest month at 6.78 inches. Moss on roofs, damp crawl spaces, clogged gutters and drainage on sloped lots all show up in inspection reports. Fixing them before listing can cost money and time, which is one reason owners with older houses consider selling as-is.

Clackamas County property tax

Clackamas County bills West Linn property owners. Under Measure 50, assessed value growth is capped at 3% a year unless the property changes, which is why the average single-family home has a taxable value of $370,342 against a real market value of $691,382.

Dates to mark:

  • December 31, 2026: last day to file a value appeal with the Property Value Appeals Board.

Yellow on the statement means your lender requested payment information and may be paying the tax for you. The county's Assessment and Taxation office takes questions at 503-655-8671, and appeal forms go to the County Clerk at 503-655-8662.

Tax rules at closing

A lien attaches to the property every July 1, so the fall bill already covers a fiscal year that began before most buyers closed. After a July 1 ownership change, the fall statement may leave out the new owner. No statement by November 1? Contact the tax collector for the amount.

State rules put late interest at 1.333% a month, beginning December 16 for the first installment. The title company usually pays or prorates the tax at closing. If you are behind, get a payoff figure before accepting an offer.

Selling for cash versus listing

Cash gives up a possibly higher list price in return for speed and fewer steps. Listing a West Linn house usually means preparing it, staging, showings, buyer financing and appraisal, and possible repair requests after inspection. A direct cash buyer purchases the house in its current state, and the title company closes it.

Weigh the two on what you would net, not just the headline price. Count repairs, agent fees, months of tax, insurance and utilities, and any HOA dues while the house waits for a buyer.

How a cash sale goes

  1. Share the address, condition and your timeline.
  2. Review the written offer, including who pays closing costs.
  3. Escrow opens at a title company, which searches for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and you receive your proceeds.

If an HOA governs the house, ask for the rules packet or resale certificate early so it is ready when escrow opens.

Schools

Nearly all of West Linn is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. West Linn High School, Athey Creek and Rosemont Ridge middle schools and four primary schools serve the city. Check your address with the district for the school your children would attend.

Preparing a wooded or sloped lot

Trees, hillsides and creeks add charm and questions in equal measure. Before you list, clear gutters and downspouts, check that water runs away from the foundation, and look for soft spots or moss on the roof. If your lot sits near a mapped habitat or water resource area, have the city's map ready so you can answer a buyer on the spot. A short written note about how the yard drains in a heavy January storm will do more for a nervous buyer than any reassurance.

Selling a house you have owned for decades

Long-time owners often hold houses that have not been remodeled in years. If that is you, compare three numbers: what an agent thinks the house would bring after updates, what it would cost to do those updates, and what a cash buyer offers for the house as it stands. Then add the months of taxes, insurance and utilities you would carry while waiting. Sometimes the as-is figure comes out closer to the listing figure than you expect, and sometimes it does not. Either way, you decide with real numbers.

Documents to bring to the title office

  • Photo ID that matches the deed.
  • Your latest tax statement.
  • Lender name and loan number for any payoff.
  • HOA rules packet or resale certificate, where one applies.
  • Papers for permits, roof work or drainage repairs.

Missing documents cause most small delays, so gather them while offers are still coming in.

Is West Linn in Clackamas County?

Yes. The county assessor and tax collector handle its property tax, and the city sits across the Willamette River from Oregon City.

What is the median home value in West Linn?

$770,200 for owner-occupied homes, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates. It is a citywide number and does not value any single property.

When are Clackamas County property taxes due?

The current-year dates are November 16, 2026, February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027. Paying in full on the first date earns a 3% discount.

Which school district covers West Linn?

Nearly all of the city is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District. Its schools include West Linn High School, Athey Creek and Rosemont Ridge middle schools and four primary schools in the city.

Do historic rules apply to my West Linn house?

They can if the house is a historic landmark or in the Willamette Historic District, where Historic Design Review applies. Ask the city planning office at 503-656-3535.
